By these are rightly noted external, empty rites and barren ceremonies with which men burden and inflate divine worship, things composed more for ostentation than for piety. Nor is it enough for men to offer such mockeries to God unless they also attribute and impute them to Him, as if He Himself had chosen and prescribed them. Certainly, the Prophet, speaking in the person of God, expostulates regarding this opinion: Is this, then, the fast that I have chosen, that a man should afflict his soul for one day and bow his head like a reed? <note>A reference to Isaiah 58:5, critiquing outward rituals that lack genuine spiritual substance.</note> After the state of Religion, the parable turns

<summary>This passage continues the critique of religious hypocrisy, arguing that empty ceremonies and rites are offered to God as a hollow imitation of true devotion, mistakenly attributed to divine command.</summary>
<keywords>hypocrisy, religious ritual, divine worship, ostentation, piety, Isaiah, Prometheus</keywords>
